title: Oil Market Report - September 2026
key_claim: US diesel/gasoil prices passed $200/bbl in early September, 94% above pre-war levels; net diesel/gasoil exports from the Gulf and Russia in August were 1.6 mb/d lower than in February, when they accounted for almost 45% of global seaborne trade; Gulf net diesel exports were 390 kb/d, just over a quarter of pre-war levels; Atlantic Basin refining margins hit records; other regions run refineries to the limit; a full Gulf supply recovery is deferred to 2027.
frame_summary: The IEA argues that the tightness of the oil market now sits in refined products, above all diesel, rather than in crude, because Gulf and Russian product exports have collapsed and inventories are the only buffer left.
verbatim_quote: Combined, net exports of diesel/gasoil exports from the Gulf and Russia in August were 1.6 mb/d lower than in February, when they accounted for almost 45% of global seaborne trade.
verbatim_list: Diesel/gasoil, which accounts for nearly 30% of global demand, saw prices in the United States surpass the $200/bbl mark in early September, 94% above pre-war levels, with Europe and Asia not far behind.
A partial offset comes from other regions, where throughputs are pushed to the limit to capture record profit margins.
Global observed oil inventories plunged by a further 95 mb in August, taking cumulative draws since February to 507 mb

title: Basket Case – The $100/bbl Diesel Crack, or How 2026 Exposed the Fragility of Global Refining

publisher: Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS)
title: Banning Gasoline Exports Will Harm U.S. Energy Security
date_evidence: Commentary by Clayton Seigle Published June 5, 2026
key_claim: Export controls would bring at best a modest, short-term, regional price cut followed by higher prices, as Gulf Coast refiners facing a glut cut runs and shift output; US product pipelines are full; allies in Europe, Japan and Korea depend on US crude and product exports as a buffer; US oil exports rose from about 10 mb/d before the war to near 14 mb/d.
frame_summary: CSIS argues that export bans backfire on the country that imposes them and damage its standing as a reliable supplier, so rational exporters should avoid them.
verbatim_quote: The following analysis contemplates a gasoline-only export ban, from which the best-case outcome is a modest, short-term, regionally concentrated price reduction, followed by higher prices as fuel manufacturers respond to upended market dynamics.
verbatim_list: Europe, Japan, South Korea, and other allies depend on U.S. crude and product exports as a strategic buffer against Middle Eastern and Russian supply disruptions.

title: FACTBOX: Countries Impose Fuel Export Restrictions During Global Energy Crisis
date_evidence: FACTBOX: Countries Impose Fuel Export Restrictions During Global Energy Crisis ... July 15, 2026
key_claim: Russia banned diesel exports from 8 July, restricted aviation fuel exports from 1 June to end-November and banned gasoline exports 1 April to 31 July; Russia supplied about 11% of world waterborne diesel in 2025; China ordered a refined-product export ban on 12 March and lifted some restrictions in late June; India imposed export taxes on diesel and jet fuel in late March, adjusted regularly; Thailand bans exports of several products since late March with limited shipments to Laos, Myanmar, the Philippines, Singapore and Vietnam; Kazakhstan plans to extend its gasoline and diesel export ban to 22 May 2027; Kyrgyzstan banned exports indefinitely.
frame_summary: OPIS documents a spreading pattern of national fuel export restrictions across producing countries, each justified by domestic shortage.
verbatim_quote: The following is a summary of countries that have taken measures in reducing fuel exports to address domestic energy shortages.
verbatim_list: In 2025, Russia was the second-largest exporter of global waterborne diesel, accounting for about 11% of all world supplies.
On March 12, China ordered a ban on refined product exports to pre-empt a potential domestic fuel shortage due to the Iran war, according to multiple wire reports.
The restriction, which was first introduced in late March, allows limited shipments to Laos, Myanmar, the Philippines, Singapore and Vietnam.
Kazakhstan’s Ministry of Energy has planned to extend its ban on gasoline and diesel fuel exports to May 22, 2027

title: Shrinking China Fuel Stockpiles Raise Chance of Export Curbs
key_claim: Chinese state-supplier gasoline stocks fell to the lowest since 2022 and diesel to a 15-month low; Beijing curbed product exports early in the war, then eased; clean product exports recovered to 2.55 million tons in July; refiners may export only on condition they keep inventories elevated; Energy Aspects sees a rising risk that Beijing restricts clean product exports to around 1.2 million tons a month in the fourth quarter.
frame_summary: Bloomberg reports that China's export permissions are conditional and reversible, tied to domestic inventories, and likely to tighten again as stocks fall.
verbatim_quote: China’s government strictly controls the amount of fuel refiners can export, and they were only allowed to resume and increase shipments on the condition that they keep inventories at elevated levels.
verbatim_list: shipments of gasoline, diesel and jet fuel, known as clean products, had recovered to a combined 2.55 million tons in July, according to the latest Chinese customs data.

“With the domestic market tightening, we see an increasing risk that Beijing could restrict monthly clean product exports to around 1.2 million tons in the fourth quarter,” said Jianan Sun, an analyst at Energy Aspects Ltd. in London.

title: Trump says administration is weighing diesel export restrictions

frame_summary: Roll Call reports that the United States is moving toward export restrictions for domestic political reasons despite analysts' warnings that it would damage its reliability as a supplier.
